cards.text: It's the eighth month of the second year of Darius, king of Persia (Ezra 4:24), and the word of the LORD comes to the prophet Zechariah son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo, with a message for the people. That's a full name AND a family tree, friend. My whole name is five letters carved into a handle.

cards.question: Before anything else, the LORD tells Zechariah how He felt about the people's fathers. True or false: He was very pleased with them.

cards.text: So Zechariah gets a message for the people from the LORD of Hosts, short enough to fit on the back of a takeout menu. I would know, because I once wrote my whole goodbye on one.

cards.question: The LORD of Hosts tells the people to return to Him. If they do, what does He promise?
Then the LORD gives the people a warning: Do not be like your ___.

cards.text: The former prophets brought the fathers a message from the LORD of Hosts: 'Turn now from your evil ways and deeds.' One line, friend, and my oven manual is FORTY pages.

cards.question: The former prophets told the fathers to turn from their evil ways and deeds. How did the fathers respond?
True or false: when the fathers ignored the former prophets, the LORD says they weren't paying attention to Him.

cards.text: Delivered, read and NOTHING, friend. They left the LORD of Hosts on read!
Then God asks two questions and just lets them sit: 'Where are your fathers now? And the prophets, do they live forever?'

cards.question: God has asked where the fathers are now and whether the prophets live forever. Next, He asks whether something of His overtook the fathers. What does He name?
True or false: when the LORD's words caught up with the fathers, they still refused to repent.
The fathers said the LORD of Hosts did to them just what He purposed, according to their ways and ___.

findings.problem: The card cites Zechariah 1:1-3, but it only tells verse 1 plus the phrase 'with a message for the people' from verse 3. It never uses verse 2, which card 2 asks about, and card 3 tells verse 3. The citation is wider than what the card tells.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke reacting to verse 4, which cards 6 to 8 already told and asked about. It tells nothing new and doesn't move the baker forward, so it works as a recap card.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards. Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: Card 6 quotes 'Turn now from your evil ways and deeds' and card 7's question repeats 'evil ways and deeds.' That gives away this card's blank ('their ways and ___', answer 'deeds'). As written, the card tests recall of a phrase already shown twice, not meaning the baker reasons out.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.
